title: Like-Denominator Fraction Word Problems
intro: Keep the unit whole visible when teaching fraction word problems.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Draw a one-foot reference strip. Show how like-sized pieces are joined or removed, then connect the drawing to the equation.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

3/8 + 7/8 = 10/8 = 5/4

Three eighth-foot parts and seven more eighth-foot parts make ten eighth-foot parts. Their size has not changed.

Each bar represents one foot. Ten shaded eighths cover one whole bar and two eighths of the next bar.

7/6 − 5/6 = 2/6 = 1/3

Check: 1/3 = 2/6, and 2/6 + 5/6 = 7/6.

Ask your student

What length does one whole represent in this story?

If your student needs help

If the student changes the denominator, return to the size of one fractional piece.
